facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against an adequate view is the structure of the debt, not today's ratios. Total leverage of 3.33x, floating-rate secured debt with no hedges, one USD 812.0 million maturity in 2030 and B-category agency ratings leave little room for error if earnings fall, and the twelve-month cash flow that supports coverage includes unusually low taxes and capital spending while acquisitions keep absorbing cash. If a 100 bp margin squeeze arrives as the quarterly gross margin trend suggests, net leverage would reach 2.69x before any buyback. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The view would strengthen if executed agreements confirmed a wide covenant cushion and baskets that limit the buyback, if acquired EBITDA showed the 2026 deals earning enough to lower leverage, and if gross margin recovered to its nine-month 2026 level of 31.58%. It would weaken if the buyback were paid from cash while acquisitions continued, if organic sales growth turned negative, if gross margin fell below the FY2024 level of 30.87%, or if the backlog in water and wastewater pumping fell below USD 325.0 million. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, DXP presents an adequate business profile supported by customer breadth, an 11.17% EBITDA margin and a growing water and wastewater platform, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-led growth funded with secured debt, floating-rate debt with one 2030 maturity and financial policy that cannot be verified. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because capital intensity is low and twelve-month free cash flow was USD 105.0 million, tempered by working capital and acquisition draws. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA growth and market access in 2029 and 2030. The primary downside path is a gross margin squeeze from input costs in a softer industrial cycle while cash goes to acquisitions and buybacks. The business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers is not established because no peer data are supplied. Further analysis would require the proxy statement, the executed agreements, acquired EBITDA and peer data. Fundamental credit analysis completed. Top risk: leverage drift from acquisition and buyback spending. Basis: calculation B01; calculation B05; calculation B06; calculation B09; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases are sufficient and current to support a credit snapshot of DXP ENTERPRISES INC as of 2026-11-05, with limits on legal, market and peer evidence that bound what creditors can conclude about covenants, pricing and relative value.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation C1

The latest quarter ended 36 days before the as-of date, and the annual report, three quarterly reports and three releases give full statements, debt, liquidity and segment disclosure for the consolidated company. Total debt of USD 839.5 million agrees between the quarterly report and the release, and cash plus revolver availability recomputes to the stated liquidity of USD 411.0 million.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C2; calculation C4; calculation C5

One conflict remains open: the annual report schedules the secured leverage covenant at 5.50x for the June and September 2026 tests, while both later quarterly reports state 5.75x, and the executed credit agreements that would settle it are not supplied. Peers, market quotes, a portfolio, numeric management guidance and the proxy statement are also absent, and the Moody's rating is dated 2025-12-31.

spans.text: # CP-1 financial foundation for DXP ENTERPRISES INC (dxpe)
## Request

DXP ENTERPRISES INC (issuer id dxpe), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the financial foundation (statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics) built from the seven supplied filings and releases and the source-readiness answer. No credit recommendation is made here.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

DXP's net debt was 2.45x twelve-month reported EBITDA at 2026-09-30, with 4.20x cash interest cover, USD 411.0 million of liquidity and no bullet maturity before 2030, so creditors' exposure is floating-rate leverage and acquisition spending, not a refinancing wall.
Basis: calculation C03; calculation C08; calculation C10; calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

Net leverage was 2.63x at 2024-12-31, 2.39x at 2025-12-31 and 2.45x at 2026-09-30: the USD 205.0 million term loan increase of December 2025 raised cash, and USD 126.2 million of 2026 cash acquisitions used it, so net debt rose 15.50% against EBITDA growth of 13.07%. The company's own secured leverage of 2.30x uses principal debt and covenant EBITDA of USD 270.0 million, so it is not comparable with these figures.

Basis: calculation C08; calculation C16; calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2

Covenant headroom is not established: the annual report and the 2026 quarterly reports state different maximum levels for the Secured Leverage Ratio, and no executed agreement is supplied. Pro forma net debt for the acquisition agreed on 2026-11-01 is also not established because its price is not stated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Leverage and its drivers

Net debt rose by USD 81.1 million between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30, from USD 523.3 million to USD 604.4 million, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA rose by USD 28.6 million to USD 247.2 million. Net leverage therefore edged up from 2.39x to 2.45x and total leverage fell from 3.78x to 3.33x. Carrying debt was almost unchanged at USD 823.2 million, so the rise in net debt is a fall in cash of USD 84.9 million: USD 126.2 million went on acquisitions in nine months against operating cash flow of USD 80.6 million.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C16; calculation C21

Against this view, the company's secured leverage ratio was 2.30x at 2026-09-30 and 2.25x at 2025-12-31, which is lower than the 2.45x here because the company measures principal debt against a wider covenant EBITDA. The view would change if acquisitions were funded with new borrowing, which the sources do not show so far, or if the new repurchase authorization of up to USD 150.0 million were used. Twelve-month EBITDA also includes the 2026 acquisitions only from their purchase dates, so the ratios are slightly high against a pro forma view that is not supplied.

Basis: calculation C20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19
### Interest cover and rate exposure

Reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 4.20x over the twelve months to 2026-09-30, 4.07x in FY2025 and 2.72x in FY2024. The FY2024 figure carries USD 9.3 million of interest for 2023 paid in 2024; without it, cover would be 3.16x, which is an Analyst Judgement shown only in the calculation. Interest expense still rose by USD 5.9 million to USD 50.2 million in nine months 2026 because the term loan was increased in December 2025.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C10; calculation C21; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30

The term loan pays Term SOFR plus 3.25% with a floor of 1.00%, its rate was 7.15% at 2026-09-30, and the annual report states no interest-rate hedges at 2025-12-31. Each 100 bp on the USD 839.5 million of principal is therefore about USD 8.4 million of annual interest, or 3.40% of twelve-month EBITDA, on the assumption that the whole balance floats and no hedge was added since year end. EBITDA growth has so far outrun the extra interest, which supports coverage.
Basis: calculation C19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow was USD 80.6 million in nine months 2026 against USD 56.5 million a year earlier and free cash flow USD 70.5 million against USD 19.5 million, but two items flatter the comparison: cash taxes paid were USD 6.6 million against USD 35.1 million, and capital expenditure was USD 10.2 million against USD 37.0 million. Working capital absorbed USD 41.9 million in 2026 against USD 60.5 million, with receivables up USD 52.6 million, and free cash flow was 37% of reported nine-month EBITDA.
Basis: calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C17; calculation C21

After USD 126.2 million of cash acquisitions, free cash flow in the nine months was negative USD 55.7 million, so the business is funding its growth from the balance sheet rather than from internally generated cash alone. The low 2026 cash taxes and capital expenditure may not repeat, and the twelve-month free cash flow of USD 105.0 million still includes them.
Basis: calculation C12; calculation C21
### Liquidity and the maturity wall

Liquidity was USD 411.0 million at 2026-09-30: USD 218.8 million of cash and USD 192.2 million of revolver availability after USD 32.8 million of letters of credit, equal to 49.93% of carrying debt. It was USD 457.3 million at 2025-12-31, so the nine-month fall in cash of USD 84.9 million was partly offset by a larger revolver. Scheduled principal is USD 2.1 million for the rest of 2026 and USD 8.5 million a year in 2027 to 2029, and USD 812.0 million falls due in 2030; the revolver now matures on 2031-07-02 where it matured on 2027-07-19 before the July 2026 agreement.

Basis: calculation C14; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85

Against this, the revolver availability is the company's own figure after letters of credit and is not shown to be a borrowing-base limit, and the threshold at which the fixed charge coverage test begins to apply is not stated, so the cushion may be smaller than the headline suggests if receivables or inventory fall.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13
### Claims outside Total Debt and definition risks

Three claims sit outside Total Debt: acquisition contingent consideration of USD 30.7 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 13.8 million at 2025-12-31 and a maximum of USD 34.0 million, finance lease liabilities of USD 20.9 million at 2025-12-31 that are not stated later, and operating lease liabilities of USD 74.7 million. Customer deposits and billings in excess of costs, a non-debt float, rose to USD 43.6 million from USD 31.1 million, with billings in excess of costs at USD 27.7 million; if projects complete, that float unwinds into cost and absorbs cash.
Basis: calculation C13; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

Management's covenant EBITDA is USD 22.8 million above reported EBITDA with no bridge, and the maximum Secured Leverage Ratio is stated at two different levels, 5.50x and 5.75x, for the June and September 2026 tests, so covenant headroom is not stated here and no covenant capacity is inferred. Interim figures are unaudited and the last twelve months are built from stubs.
Basis: calculation C20; Source readiness (CP-0)

## Gaps

The maximum Secured Leverage Ratio for the June and September 2026 tests is 5.50 to 1.00 in the annual report schedule but less than 5.75 to 1.00 in the second-quarter and third-quarter reports, and no executed credit agreement is supplied, so covenant headroom cannot be stated as one figure. Severity High. Action: obtain the executed term loan agreement and the December 2025 amendment.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dxpe-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; Source readiness (CP-0)

Management's covenant EBITDA of USD 270.0 million for the twelve months to 2026-09-30 is USD 22.8 million above reported EBITDA and USD 15.6 million above Adjusted EBITDA, and no source bridges the measures, so the company's secured leverage of 2.30x cannot be rebuilt line by line from reported figures. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the covenant compliance certificate or the agreement's EBITDA definition schedule.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85; calculation C20

Pro forma EBITDA for the five acquisitions of 2026 is not supplied, although the third-quarter report gives pro forma sales of USD 1,699.9 million against reported USD 1,685.3 million for nine months, so twelve-month EBITDA includes the acquired businesses only from their purchase dates and the leverage ratios are slightly overstated against a pro forma view. Severity Medium. Action: obtain pro forma EBITDA for the acquisitions.

The security package of the term loan and its ranking beyond receivables and inventory are not stated, the revolver's floor is not stated, the filing states carrying value only for total debt and not for each instrument, and the promissory note's security and ranking are not stated, so the debt stack ranks the revolver ahead of the term loan on shared collateral only. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the term loan agreement and the intercreditor terms.

The price of the agreement of 2026-11-01 to acquire MDS of Michigan, LLC and any purchases under the repurchase program authorized on 2026-10-28 are not stated, so the pro forma net debt and pro forma net leverage after these events are not established. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the purchase price and the repurchase activity from the next filing.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

Finance lease liabilities are not stated at 2026-09-30 (they were USD 20.9 million at 2025-12-31), so lease-adjusted leverage at the latest date is not calculable. Severity Low. Action: obtain the lease note of the next annual report or a quarterly lease disclosure.

Restricted cash is printed as a dash at 2025-12-31 and has no line at 2026-09-30, and the 2024 balance of USD 0.091 million was excluded from Cash & Equivalents; at 2026-09-30 cash and restricted cash in the cash flow statement equal the Cash line, so none is implied. Severity Low. Action: none needed.

The fourth quarter of 2025 is not reported on its own, so its sales of USD 527.4 million and EBITDA of USD 57.5 million are calculated as FY2025 less nine months 2025 and labelled calculated. Severity Low. Action: none needed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C21

The statements for FY2023 are in the annual report but were not extracted, so the trend rests on FY2024, FY2025 and the 2026 periods, and no FY2023 balance sheet is in the documents supplied. Severity Low. Action: extract FY2023 income statement and cash flow only if a longer trend is needed.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68

No year-end secured leverage ratio or covenant EBITDA is supplied for FY2024, and no covenant EBITDA for FY2025, so the company-reported series in the metrics table starts at 2025-12-31 for the ratio and 2026-09-30 for covenant EBITDA. Severity Low. Action: none needed for this snapshot.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2

Capital expenditure is stated in total only; no maintenance and growth split is stated. The interim statements and the quarterly reports are unaudited and the filings do not say whether the auditor reviewed them. Severity Low. Action: none needed.

The Total Leverage Ratio that sets the term loan's excess cash flow prepayment, which is 50% of excess cash flow falling to 25% at or below 3.00 to 1.00 and nil at or below 2.50 to 1.00, is not stated in the filings, so whether any mandatory prepayment is due from 2026 cash flow is not established. Severity Low. Action: obtain the agreement's definition of Total Leverage Ratio and the company's computation.

Interest-rate hedging after 2025-12-31 is stated only by reference to the annual report, which reports no hedges, so the rate-sensitivity figure assumes none. Severity Low. Action: confirm in the next annual report.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C19

spans.text: # CP-1A business and transaction facts for DXP ENTERPRISES INC (dxpe)
## Request

DXP ENTERPRISES INC (issuer id dxpe), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the business, transaction, ownership and operating-model facts, and the governance and shareholder-behavior assessment, drawn from the seven supplied filings and releases and the source-readiness answer. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery view is given.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| EX-99.1_2026-08-05_earningsrelease6302026.htm.jsonl | Earnings press release for the second quarter of 2026 (Exhibit 99.1) | 2026-08-05 | 6d154d2d8605fdb9abb6da2ab17ed2ed1363c8da5b1cd9a1ff2db3ea0cf9c96c | Read to confirm the second-quarter acquisition and covenant statements; no figure from it is used |

| EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl | Earnings press release for the third quarter of 2026 (Exhibit 99.1) | 2026-11-05 | 7fc5ad335ae78b4ce865ab4ec5f61033f2b042958c1ba4a250444be1733b49a2 | Management's stated total debt, covenant EBITDA and secured leverage at 2026-09-30; management commentary on acquisitions |
Supplied module answer used by this module:
| Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness (CP-0) | 69fa01cceaaf10466a0146bbb22884307f5d270a0c1dbefebc6142e13a9c6b85 | Source set, perimeter, covenant-level conflict, missing documents (proxy statement, executed agreements) and cutoff |
## Findings
### Bottom line

DXP is an acquisitive, listed industrial distributor with no sponsor or parent named in the sources, so creditors rely on management restraint: USD 153.6 million went on acquisitions in nine months 2026 and a USD 150.0 million buyback was authorized on 2026-10-28.
Basis: calculation A01; calculation A08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

Operating risk is moderate: no customer reaches 10% of sales, nine-month organic growth was 9.3%, and USD 411.0 million of liquidity sits against USD 839.5 million of debt. The view stays cautious because the chief executive's holding and the board's independence are not established and acquired earnings are not disclosed, so leverage after the deals cannot be tested.

Basis: calculation A04; calculation A11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

Growth is partly bought, which makes acquisition discipline the central credit variable. Sales rose 13.19% in nine months 2026 and organic sales rose 9.26%; acquired businesses supplied 8.27% of sales and 33.88% of Innovative Pumping Solutions sales in the third quarter, and 18 businesses cost USD 407.7 million across 2024, 2025 and nine months 2026.

Basis: calculation A03; calculation A04; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

Acquisitions outran free cash flow and were met from cash that the December 2025 term loan increase appears to have supplied. Free cash flow of USD 70.5 million covered 55.84% of the USD 126.2 million spent in nine months 2026 on acquisitions net of cash acquired, and the USD 205.0 million of new term loan commitments preceded the spending. The filings do not state what the loan proceeds were for, so this link is an analyst interpretation.
Basis: calculation A02; calculation A08; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 83; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

Acquired earnings are not disclosed, so the leverage effect of the acquisition program cannot be tested from the filings. The acquisition notes give consideration, goodwill, intangibles and sales but no acquired EBITDA, and management's covenant EBITDA of USD 270.0 million includes pro forma acquisition effects that the filings do not bridge; the company's 2.30x secured leverage rests on that figure.

Basis: calculation A11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2; Source readiness (CP-0)

Shareholder returns have been restrained so far, but the new authorization is large against free cash flow. Repurchases fell from USD 54.7 million in 2023 to USD 28.8 million in 2024, USD 17.0 million in 2025 and nothing in nine months 2026, and USD 68.0 million of the earlier authorization was left unused when that program ended in August 2026. The new USD 150.0 million program equals 142.91% of twelve-month free cash flow of USD 105.0 million and 68.55% of cash, and the term loan limits restricted payments with some baskets open only below stated leverage levels, but the basket sizes and thresholds are not supplied, so whether covenants would limit it is not established.

Basis: calculation A08; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 92; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; Source readiness (CP-0)

Control and governance cannot be verified because the proxy statement is not supplied. The chief executive has been Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer since 1996 and acquired a controlling interest in the predecessor company in 1986, but his current holding, the board's independence and its committee membership are not stated. Related-party dealings are small: USD 2.3 million of 2025 lease expense went to entities the chief executive and family control, 0.50% of selling, general and administrative expense, and the Audit Committee reviews related-party transactions above USD 120,000.
Basis: calculation A10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102

Operating risk is moderate and sits with suppliers and end markets, not customers. No customer reached 10% of sales in three years, over 90% of sales are products and 96.18% of 2025 sales were in the United States, but manufacturers can cancel distribution authorizations on little or no notice, part of revenue depends on oil, gas and petrochemical spending, and Supply Chain Services contracts can be cancelled on little or no notice. Backlog in Innovative Pumping Solutions was USD 325.0 million at the end of 2025, 11.2% above a year earlier.

Basis: calculation A06; calculation A12; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32

The group structure is simple and all outstanding debt is secured, but Canadian cash flows are outside the term loan guarantee. The issuer borrows the term loan, wholly owned material subsidiaries other than the Canadian ones guarantee it, and Canadian subsidiaries guarantee the revolver obligations of the Canadian borrowers but not the term loan; Canada was 3.35% of nine-month 2026 sales, so the gap is narrow.
Basis: calculation A06; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20

No creditor-adverse behavior is documented, though the record is incomplete. The sources show no dividend recapitalization, uptier, drop-down or non-pro-rata exchange, and the one term loan amendment of the period was agreed with lenders to add debt and adjust covenant dates. The annual report also says the company has at times been unable to meet covenants under earlier facilities and obtained waivers, without dates or detail.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is balance-sheet strength. Liquidity of USD 411.0 million is 48.47x the USD 8.5 million of scheduled principal due in each of 2027 to 2029, the company's own secured leverage of 2.30x is far below its maximum of 5.50x or 5.75x, S&P raised the rating to B+ in July 2026, no common dividend is paid, and total debt fell by USD 7.3 million in nine months 2026 even as acquisitions continued. Organic growth of 9.26% also shows the acquired businesses are not masking weak demand.

Basis: calculation A04; calculation A11; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dxpe-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 32

The view would soften if a proxy statement showed a majority-independent board and a modest insider holding, if acquired EBITDA and purchase multiples showed deals priced below current leverage, if the executed agreements showed restricted-payment baskets too small to take the USD 150.0 million program at current leverage, and if repurchases stayed inside free cash flow. It would harden if repurchases were paid from cash while acquisitions continued, if leverage rose without matching earnings, if a fall in acquisition sales exposed weaker organic growth, if a major manufacturer withdrew an authorization, or if the baskets proved large enough to fund the whole program while leverage stayed where it is.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so the chief executive's holding, the board's independence and any other large holder are not established; a large insider stake would raise key-person and related-party risk while an independent board would lessen it, so the governance conclusion could move either way.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 102; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Acquired EBITDA, purchase multiples and per-deal terms are not disclosed, so the conclusion on acquisition discipline rests on spending and sales contribution only; deals bought at high multiples or with weak margins would make it adverse.

- The executed credit agreements are not supplied, so the size of restricted-payment, investment and incremental-debt baskets and the leverage levels that open them are unknown; the shareholder-return conclusion treats the USD 150.0 million program as unconstrained by anything quantified, and a tight basket would lessen the concern.

The sources show no new notes or bonds in the period; DXP's two debt changes were bank-facility amendments. spans.text: # CP-2 fundamental credit synthesis for DXP ENTERPRISES INC (dxpe)
## Request

DXP ENTERPRISES INC (issuer id dxpe), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the integrated fundamental credit view built from the seven supplied filings and releases and the three earlier module answers, covering business risk, financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing is given.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

DXP is an adequate fundamental credit whose main exposure is financial policy, not liquidity: broad customers, an 11.17% EBITDA margin and USD 411.0 million of liquidity protect debt service, while acquisitions and a new USD 150.0 million buyback could push floating-rate secured leverage up.
Basis: calculation B01; calculation B03; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

Net leverage was 2.45x at 2026-09-30 and cash interest cover 4.20x, and pro forma net debt for the acquisition agreed on 2026-11-01 and for the new buyback is not established. The view rests on ownership, a covenant level and acquired earnings that the documents do not settle.
Basis: calculation B02; calculation B03; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

Earnings are broad and growing, which is the main support for debt service. Twelve-month sales were USD 2,212.7 million, up 9.74% on FY2025, and reported EBITDA rose 13.07% to USD 247.2 million, lifting the margin from 10.84% to 11.17%; no customer reached 10% of sales and organic sales rose 9.26% in nine months 2026.
Basis: calculation B01; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21

Leverage is moderate but has drifted up because growth is paid for with cash. Net debt rose 15.50% to USD 604.4 million while twelve-month EBITDA rose 13.07%, so net leverage moved from 2.39x at 2025-12-31 to 2.45x and total leverage is 3.33x; the company's own secured leverage of 2.30x is lower because it uses principal debt and covenant EBITDA of USD 270.0 million. These figures are before the acquisition agreed on 2026-11-01 and the new buyback; pro forma net debt and leverage are not established, because the price and any purchase are not stated.

Basis: calculation B02; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2

Debt service is covered with room. Cash interest cover is 4.20x, liquidity is 48.47x the USD 8.5 million of principal due each year to 2029, and each 100 bp on the floating-rate term loan costs about USD 8.4 million, or 3.40% of EBITDA; with no hedges in place, a 200 bp rise would cut cover to 3.27x if the whole balance floats.

Basis: calculation B03; calculation B04; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34

Refinancing risk is concentrated in one year. USD 812.0 million, 96.72% of principal and 3.28x EBITDA, falls due on 2030-10-13, while the revolver now runs to 2031-07-02; S&P raised the rating to B+ in July 2026 and Moody's rated the corporate credit B1 at the end of 2025, but no market quotes are supplied, so pricing and market access are not established.

Basis: calculation B05; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

Free cash flow is positive but flattered, so growth is not self-funded. Twelve-month free cash flow of USD 105.0 million compares with USD 54.0 million in FY2025 and benefits from cash taxes of USD 6.6 million against USD 35.1 million and capital expenditure of USD 10.2 million against USD 37.0 million in nine months; after USD 126.2 million of cash acquisitions the nine-month figure was negative USD 55.7 million, and free cash flow covered only 58.52% of cash acquisitions from 2024 to nine months 2026.

Basis: calculation B06; calculation B07; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

Gross margin is the pressure point: it fell each quarter of 2026, from 32.3% to 31.8% to 30.7%, and the third quarter was 0.70 percentage points below a year earlier, which the company ties to higher input costs. Operating leverage hid this, because selling, general and administrative expense fell to 21.81% of third-quarter sales from 22.88%, but a further 100 bp of EBITDA margin loss would cost USD 22.1 million, 8.95% of EBITDA, and lift net leverage to 2.69x on unchanged net debt.

Basis: calculation B09; 10-Q_2026-03-31_dxpe-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dxpe-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

Financial policy is the swing factor for creditors. The company pays no common dividend and bought no shares in nine months 2026, but it authorized a USD 150.0 million buyback on 2026-10-28, equal to 142.91% of twelve-month free cash flow, while its chief executive's holding and the board's independence are not established; Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as Medium.
Basis: calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

Business risk is moderate. Service Centers supply 64.23% of nine-month 2026 sales and depend on manufacturers who can cancel authorizations on little notice, part of revenue follows oil, gas and petrochemical spending, and tariffs and vendor price increases press on margin; against that, water and wastewater pumping now supplies 24.06% of sales at a 17.70% operating margin, with USD 325.0 million of backlog at the end of 2025.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against an adequate view is the structure of the debt, not today's ratios. Total leverage of 3.33x, floating-rate secured debt with no hedges, one USD 812.0 million maturity in 2030 and B-category agency ratings leave little room for error if earnings fall, and the twelve-month cash flow that supports coverage includes unusually low taxes and capital spending while acquisitions keep absorbing cash. If a 100 bp margin squeeze arrives as the quarterly gross margin trend suggests, net leverage would reach 2.69x before any buyback.
Basis: calculation B02; calculation B04; calculation B05; calculation B06; calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

The view would strengthen if executed agreements confirmed a wide covenant cushion and baskets that limit the buyback, if acquired EBITDA showed the 2026 deals earning enough to lower leverage, and if gross margin recovered to its nine-month 2026 level of 31.58%. It would weaken if the buyback were paid from cash while acquisitions continued, if organic sales growth turned negative, if gross margin fell below the FY2024 level of 30.87%, or if the backlog in water and wastewater pumping fell below USD 325.0 million. Strength in liquidity of USD 411.0 million would still delay any liquidity event, so the weakening path is leverage and refinancing, not a near-term cash shortfall.

Basis: calculation B01; calculation B09; calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; Source readiness (CP-0)

### Company description

DXP distributes maintenance, repair and operating products to industrial customers from a branch network in the United States and Canada, and also engineers custom pump packages and runs customers' procurement and storerooms. Service Centers supplied 68.10% of FY2025 sales, Innovative Pumping Solutions 19.36% and Supply Chain Services 12.54%, and sales grew from a business founded in 1908 to USD 2,016.4 million in FY2025 largely through acquisitions, 64 of them since 2004.

Basis: calculation B08; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99

The model supports debt service because products are replacement and consumable items sold to a wide base, with no customer at 10% of sales, but it ties up working capital: receivables rose USD 52.6 million in nine months 2026. Cash flow is therefore durable in a stable economy and sensitive to industrial activity and to supplier terms.
Basis: calculation B06; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4
### Ownership and group structure

DXP is a listed Texas corporation with no sponsor or parent named in the documents. Its chairman, president and chief executive has led it since 1996 and acquired control of the predecessor company in 1986, but his current holding, the board's independence and the identity of the Series B preferred holders are not established; related-party leases are small at 0.50% of selling, general and administrative expense.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 100

Material wholly owned subsidiaries other than the Canadian ones guarantee the term loan, and the U.S. ones guarantee the revolver, so Canada, at 3.35% of nine-month 2026 sales, sits outside the term loan guarantee. Leverage tolerance has been moderate, with net leverage between 2.39x and 2.45x, but acquisition appetite is high at USD 407.7 million across 18 businesses since 2024, and creditors' protection rests on covenants because no outside equity backstop is shown.
Basis: calculation B02; calculation B07; calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is transactional and cyclical, not contracted. Customers buy on purchase orders, DXP traditionally has no long-term customer contracts, and the Supply Chain Services contracts that exist can be cancelled on little or no notice; demand follows industrial production, maintenance budgets and energy capital spending, so sales rose 11.89% in FY2025 and 13.19% in nine months 2026, of which 9.26% was organic.

Basis: calculation B01; calculation B08; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24

Pricing power is moderate. Management says it has kept strong margins despite vendor price increases, and the nine-month gross margin held at 31.58%, but the third quarter shows a lag: input costs cut the gross margin by 65 basis points. Backlog in Innovative Pumping Solutions of USD 325.0 million at the end of 2025 gives some visibility for that segment, though backlog can be delayed or cancelled.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

Cost of sales is 68.42% of nine-month 2026 sales, and after product cost labor is the largest expense. Selling, general and administrative expense of 22.65% of sales is mostly payroll, rent, insurance and professional fees, which are semi-fixed: they produced operating leverage in the third quarter, when the ratio fell to 21.81% from 22.88%, and they would work against margin if volumes fell.
Basis: calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure because capex and acquisitions are discretionary, but not fully against input-cost inflation or adverse mix: the quarterly gross margin fell from 32.3% to 30.7% during 2026, and a further 100 bp of EBITDA margin would cost USD 22.1 million, 8.95% of twelve-month EBITDA.
Basis: calculation B09; 10-Q_2026-03-31_dxpe-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-06-30_dxpe-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28
### Capital intensity and cash flow conversion

Capital intensity is low, at 2.00% of FY2025 sales and 0.60% in nine months 2026, and operating lease liabilities are USD 74.7 million, so most of EBITDA can convert to cash; free cash flow was 37.17% of nine-month EBITDA and 12.75% of carrying debt over twelve months. Conversion is flattered by cash taxes of USD 6.6 million in nine months 2026 against USD 35.1 million a year earlier, and working capital absorbed USD 41.9 million.
Basis: calculation B06; calculation B09; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4

EBITDA translates into durable free cash flow for debt service and for some deleveraging, but not for both growth by acquisition and a large buyback at once: capex flexibility is high, yet acquisitions, contingent consideration of USD 30.7 million and the buyback all draw on the same cash, and no seasonal pattern is stated.
Basis: calculation B07; calculation B10; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is high: the market is highly fragmented, DXP ranked 17th among U.S. distributors of these products, and several competitors have greater resources, so pricing is a constant constraint on margin and on the cash flow that services debt.

The threat of new entrants is moderate and the threat of substitutes comes mainly from manufacturers selling direct, which the company lists as a risk to sales and earnings; neither is shown to have hurt results, so the credit effect is a monitoring item.

Buyer power is moderate: no customer is large, but customers can consolidate suppliers and DXP has few long-term contracts, which limits pricing. Supplier power is high, because manufacturers can cancel authorizations on little notice and set the prices that DXP must pass through, which is the main route to margin and availability risk.
### Macro and policy factors

Two factors matter to credit. Economic conditions drive volumes and the cost of USD 839.5 million of floating-rate debt, and trade policy raises vendor costs: the company says new and expanded tariffs disrupt supply chains and that their effect cannot be predicted. Social and technological factors do not appear to be primary credit drivers on the provided materials.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are average: USD 2,212.7 million of twelve-month sales and a 17th ranking among U.S. distributors give shock-absorbing scale, and management calls DXP the largest North American distributor of rotating equipment, but there is no market-share data. Competitive advantage is average, resting on first-tier distribution, technical service and engineered pump packages, while authorizations are cancellable and no switching-cost data are supplied. Business diversification is average: customers and geography are broad, with 96.18% of FY2025 sales in the United States, but suppliers, end markets and the acquisition engine concentrate risk.
Basis: calculation B01; calculation B08; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26

Cost and capex flexibility is strong, because capital expenditure is 0.60% to 2.00% of sales and acquisitions are discretionary, although selling, general and administrative expense is semi-fixed. Margin stability is average: the gross margin was 30.87% in FY2024, 31.54% in FY2025 and 31.58% in nine months 2026, with a 30.7% third quarter. Free cash flow stability is average: it was USD 77.1 million in FY2024, USD 54.0 million in FY2025 and USD 105.0 million over twelve months, moving with taxes, capital spending and working capital.
Basis: calculation B06; calculation B07; calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 68; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70

Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the B+ and B1 ratings and a revolver to 2031 help, but 96.72% of principal matures in 2030 and no quotes are supplied. Liquidity is strong at USD 411.0 million. Financial policy and governance is average and could move to weak if the buyback proceeds from cash while deals continue, because ownership is unverified and the covenant level conflicts across documents.
Basis: calculation B03; calculation B05; calculation B10; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33

The main credit supports are customer breadth, liquidity and rising coverage; the main constraints are secured floating-rate leverage of 3.33x, acquisition-funded growth and a single 2030 maturity. The trend is steady in earnings, softer in gross margin and flat to slightly higher in net leverage, from 2.39x to 2.45x, and pro forma net debt for the acquisition agreed on 2026-11-01 and for the new buyback is not established. Missing datapoints are acquired EBITDA, the executed agreements, the proxy statement and peer data.
Basis: calculation B02; calculation B05; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months management expects to finish 2026 strongly with momentum into 2027 and, in the annual report, expected continued growth in 2026, but it gives no numeric guidance. Tailwinds are the full-year effect of the August 2026 Mequipco purchase and the agreed MDS of Michigan purchase, water and wastewater project demand, acquired businesses owned under twelve months that already added USD 48.8 million of sales in the third quarter, and operating leverage; headwinds are the 2026 fall in gross margin, tariff and input-cost inflation, a cash interest bill of USD 58.8 million over twelve months on unhedged debt, and the pull on cash from acquisitions and the buyback.

Basis: calculation B03; calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_earningsrelease9302026.htm.jsonl, page 2

Over three to five years the term loan and revolver mature in 2030 and 2031, amortization is only 0.25% a quarter and the excess cash flow sweep, 50% falling to 25% below a Total Leverage Ratio of 3.00x and to nil at 2.50x or lower, adds little at current leverage, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth rather than repayment. The sector tailwind is infrastructure and water demand; the headwinds are industrial and energy cycles and tariff policy.

### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a slowdown in industrial production and energy capital spending while vendors raise prices faster than DXP can pass them on, which the third-quarter margin already hints at. The first operational break is gross margin and Service Centers volume, 64.23% of sales, with Innovative Pumping Solutions projects deferred or cancelled from the USD 325.0 million backlog.

Basis: calculation B08; calculation B09; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28

The financial transmission is EBITDA: each 100 bp of margin lost costs USD 22.1 million, 8.95% of twelve-month EBITDA, and lifts net leverage from 2.45x to 2.69x on unchanged net debt, an Assumption-Based sensitivity and not a forecast; pro forma net debt for the acquisition agreed on 2026-11-01 and for the new buyback is not established. Falling receivables and inventory would release cash, but customer deposits and billings in excess of costs of USD 43.6 million would unwind, and cash interest would stay near USD 58.8 million because the debt is unhedged.
Basis: calculation B02; calculation B03; calculation B09; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3

Liquidity of USD 411.0 million is 48.47x annual scheduled principal, the revolver fixed charge coverage test of 1.00x applies only in a compliance period triggered by low availability and stood at 2.98x, and the stated secured leverage of 2.30x is far below the stated maximum of 5.50x or 5.75x, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress. Management's levers are to stop acquisitions and the buyback, cut capital spending and release working capital; the stress falls on leverage and on the 2030 refinancing, where USD 812.0 million is 3.28x EBITDA today.

Basis: calculation B03; calculation B05; 10-K_2025-12-31_dxpe-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dxpe-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33
### Overall credit view

Overall, DXP presents an adequate business profile supported by customer breadth, an 11.17% EBITDA margin and a growing water and wastewater platform, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-led growth funded with secured debt, floating-rate debt with one 2030 maturity and financial policy that cannot be verified. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because capital intensity is low and twelve-month free cash flow was USD 105.0 million, tempered by working capital and acquisition draws. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on EBITDA growth and market access in 2029 and 2030. The primary downside path is a gross margin squeeze from input costs in a softer industrial cycle while cash goes to acquisitions and buybacks. The business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers is not established because no peer data are supplied. Further analysis would require the proxy statement, the executed agreements, acquired EBITDA and peer data. Fundamental credit analysis completed.
